heading: Mapping: Tac
summary: The same Converter and the same plan in the browser and on native targets. A view addresses a service, the service asks for the converter with Needs, and the converter carries the field plan.
body:
Select a language tab and copy the page, the component view and the two role files. JavaScript, TypeScript and Dart bundle for the web. Go, F#, Java and Ruby bundle for the web as WebAssembly. Swift, Kotlin, C# and Rust stage their native hosts. The view reads {catalog.title} from the service. A view can read only from a service (ADR 0030). The browser services ask for the converter with Needs: a Needs field, a `#[Needs]` `attr_reader` in Ruby, or a constructor parameter in F#. A converter needs no behavior context and no Setup, so Tachyon builds it and the service only maps. The native services stay plain types, as they do elsewhere in Tac. The compiler finds the annotated converter file and adds it to the same compile unit.

The annotation and its options are the same as in Yon. The converter is the same contract too, with a protocol in Swift, and a method body fails the build with TY1308. The previous section runs them in a full example. Only the realm is different. The role folder is client/converters (ADR 0031). A mapping reaches no adapter and needs no authorization, because it reads only the argument that it was given. It is the only data annotation that cannot leave the running process. Tac stays client-rendered. It uses only public TAC_ configuration, never private Yon credentials.
